v1_changes: ATH-11: core block FIRST by default in every session of every family (after the warm-up); about 2 core exercises (VOL-17); the user can move it after the plyos, after strength or to the end. Replaces the v0 'core primer only in athletic programs (tier 3b)' and 'core on optional days for hypertrophy' rules.

UNI-11 + ORD-06: pairing rule is slot-level and universal for any session that mixes lower and upper work - hip-dominant (posterior lower) goes with a push (anterior upper), knee-dominant goes with a pull - to avoid bleed-over. Applies to full body, bootcamps, athletic days, strength compressions and hybrid days.

ORD-06: BOOTCAMP 1 Tue/Fri ('Bilateral HD' -> 'Vertical Pull' -> 'Unilateral KD' -> 'Horizontal Push') was a mistake; corrected to hinge + horizontal push, single-leg squat + vertical pull. G2 grammar redefined.
UNI-11: the vertical vector is no longer 'free' - it follows the lower pattern it is paired with. G8 athletic themed days and HYBRID Saturday re-wired.

UNI-06: same-pattern days (squat + lunge) for physique / growth goals; cross-pattern days (squat + single-leg hinge) for bootcamp, fat loss, general fitness and athletes (default). Athletic default switched from the BYOP same-pattern grammar to cross-pattern; same-pattern kept as a variant for growth-focused athletes.
ORD-01: row before pulldown (horizontal before vertical) everywhere. The FAT BURN / 4 TRACKS / boxing pulldown-first order is not followed; open question 22 closed.
ORD-02: 'the work' (the day's main lift) comes first even when it is vertical (overhead-press weeks).
ORD-03: power before strength everywhere; the HYBRID 'strength before OLY' order is not followed; open question 18 closed.
ORD-04: calves first / side raises first only when that muscle is the client's priority; default position is the end of the session.

ORD-05: supersets are a fatigue and time tool with four use cases: short session, advanced athlete who needs more stimulus, off-season VO2max / mitochondrial work, beginner who does not fatigue. Default for an intermediate with enough time is straight sets.

ORD-07: 'the work' (main lift, 1 RIR) / 'the accessory' (supporting lift, 2 RIR) / 'the nuance' (weak point, unilateral or variation, MAX) / 'the survival' (isolation or joint health, done no matter what) confirmed as the strength backbone; strength cut order changed so the survival is never cut first.
ORD-08: a warm-up is always written (5 min any cardio + A March/Skip/Run or mobility); A-drills never count as volume.
ORD-09: fighters' cardio-first blocks are real aerobic blocks, not warm-ups.
ORD-10: optional days can be add-ons or separate days; separate is preferred.
ORD-11: Focus 1 and Focus 2 may hit the same muscle, 2-3 sets each, to bring a priority muscle up to its weekly target.

VOL-07: set-addition order (first exercise of the day first, then the next: 2/2/2 -> 3/2/2 -> 3/3/2 -> 3/3/3 -> 4/3/3); 3-4 exercises per muscle group per day; small muscles at the end get extra volume as a bonus exercise. Retires the v0 'at most 2 exercises per muscle per session'.

VOL-08 / VOL-16 / VOL-17 / UNI-09: exercise caps and session lengths by population (resistance-only 5-7, 45 min ~5, 60 min ~6-7, 75-90 min ~8-9; field athletes off-season up to 10-12 = 2 core + 2-4 plyo/ballistic + 2-3 Olympic/power + 3-4 resistance; athletes/bodybuilders/powerlifters ~90 min, max 2 h; general/weight loss 45-60 min). Replaces the v0 60-minute anchor for everyone.
VOL-17: calves 3 sets on every leg day; rear delts get their own sets (rear-delt station on pull days); about 2 core exercises.

PER-04: no axial (spinal) loading twice a week per pattern - one axial squat and one axial hinge a week; the second squat exposure is leg press / belt squat (EQ-11); the second hinge exposure is non-axial (pool PROPOSED).
PER-04: second weekly exposure of a slot uses a different exercise (confirmed), now constrained by the axial rule.
PRG-03: bootcamp = 4, 5 or 6 sessions a week, timed circuits of 5-7 stations x 3-5 rounds x 30-50 s, 35-45 min total. Bootcamp circuit day types added.
PRG-02: PPL weekdays are flexible (the athlete chooses).

PRG-05: level names L1 / L2 / L3; novice = newby (same thing) = under about 6-12 months of training; intermediate = consistent for over a year; more than 6-12 months off = body treated as L1 (skills return fast); ex-pros start L1 briefly.
PRG-06: one consistent algorithm for rep, set and volume progression across every level and model; templates carry no level-specific rep schemes.

PRG-07: notation '12/10/8 -20' = pyramid (12 mid weight, 10 heavier, 8 heaviest) then drop to a light 20-rep set (4 working sets); '10/10' = per side on unilateral work (1 set); '10/10' on a bilateral lift = two sets of 10.

FIX-03 / ATH-13: generic, understandable program and day names; 'JUSTICE LEAGUE' -> 'Athletic Performance - Non-Competitive' (weekend warriors, adults and youth). NO ACCESS meaning still pending (PRG-01 skipped).

ATH-07: aerobic sessions per week by population: 3 general / fat loss, 2 athletes in season, 4 aesthetics / bodybuilders + long walks after workouts (for the whole Muscle & Physique family; verification pass 2). Open question 8 closed except colour rules.

ATH-10 / ATH-09: every athletic session family carries Olympic work (L1: DB/KB snatch, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls / hang cleans; L2-L3: full lifts); youth may lift from the floor; older clients get few plyos unless they ask; no sex-based rules.

ATH-01 / ATH-02 / CAT-10: sport dial rebuilt on ground-contact time (long ground contact -> more ballistics, short -> more plyos); programs start more ballistic and become more plyometric; the plyo method progression (receive & pause -> receive then create -> repeated) is not a 'zone'.
ATH-04: boxers / strikers - pressing and arm volume is reduced (never cut to zero) when punching volume is high. v0 'H push and V pull removed' rule retired.
ATH-05 / EQ-06: no medball work for aesthetics / bodybuilders except as warm-up; medballs never over 20 lb.

ATH-06: COD stays for every athlete, tiered by turn angle; open question 12 closed. Generated athletic weeks carry COD from 60 min (hip days from 60, knee days from 75, 3-day S1 from 60 - verification pass 2).
ATH-12: contrast / French contrast for L2+ athletes off-season, about 78-85%, no rest inside the complex; open question 23 closed (keep the immediate format).
PER-05: deload = about half the sets, same exercises, lighter (or 3+ RIR), no buy-out or finisher; architecture kept. Open question 21 closed.

PER-01 / PER-02 / PER-03 / PER-07: plan shapes moved to 06 (4-6 week maintenance at ~50-70% volume, 8-week = 4 adapt + 4 drive, 12-week = 2-4 acclimate + 4-6 drive + hardest last weeks, week-by-week and yearly modes); A/B lead-lift weeks optional for variety seekers; tests by checkbox at block start or none.

UNI-02 / UNI-03 / UNI-10 / CAT-13: laterality dial added to lower (and upper) slots - bilateral:unilateral share from 90/10 to 10/90 by athlete, phase and pain; in season minimal bilateral; contralateral loading pulls into the hip (COD athletes), ipsilateral helps out of the hip (sprint acceleration).

VOL-09 / VOL-10 / UNI-01 / LIB-16: credit the exercise picked: helpers 0.25, dips 0.5 triceps / 0.5 chest, 10/10 unilateral = 1 set, athletic patterns (plyos, throws, Olympic lifts, sprints) never count toward muscle sets - so ballistic fills of the BASEBALL 'calfs' slot no longer count as calf sets.

EQ-01 / EQ-07 / EQ-08 / EQ-12 / LIB-09: no bands and no variable resistance in any pool (banded pulldowns, band assisted pull-ups, band chops removed); 'Camporini Deadlift' and 'strap rotating in/out' removed; 'Pull under' = lat pull-over.
VOL-10/VOL-11: 40-rep sets and AMRAPs only in CrossFit / hybrid styles.

All 30 generator split templates (2-6 days x 6 families) regenerated programmatically with these rules, plus variants (upper/lower, PPL x2, same-pattern athletic, BASEBALL Parts, in-season, bootcamp circuits). Each carries recomputed checks: weekly pattern frequency, slot-level pairing (UNI-11), axial budget (PER-04), core-first and H-before-V order, power before strength, exercise caps and a time estimate.

The floor of 10 is read on groups.

**Focus muscle 1 and Focus muscle 2** replace the intake "priority muscle": +1 to +3 weekly sets each (default +2), first in their session, delivered through their own exercises, then the optional day's Focus 1 / Focus 2 slots.

**Time vs minimums replaces the time-overflow rule**: when the chosen days x minutes cannot hold the minimums, the plan says so up front and offers another day or the length that fits; if the user keeps the time, fewer groups are trained directly; supersets are recommended; the stairway climbs on every trained group. Every template is checked at week 1 (with the floor) and at an 8-week peak (8.7.1).

**Superset recommendations**: every main day lists its eligible pairs, marked "recommended" (the day also fits in straight sets) or "needed" (it fits only with them) - "Recommend doing supersets so that it's a faster workout".

**Plan editing**: every station carries a block id (warm-up, core, skill, athletic, Olympic, resistance, focus, conditioning); the user or coach may switch a day's athletic, Olympic, skill, core, focus or conditioning block off, and add or remove exercises or whole blocks. Toggles change no muscle-set number.

**No check-in, nothing stored.** The v1.1 check-in hooks (the step table, effort 10 = hold -1 set, the block-at-risk prompt, the maintenance end prompt, test reminders, the week-by-week mode) are retired; the plan follows its planned stairway (approved) and prints a self-adjust guide.
**Set addition approved**: Monday's first exercise, then Thursday's; a small muscle's bonus exercise goes on the optional day, or on a day that already trains it, never as its only exercise that day.
**Calendar**: the easy week after a block is a recommendation, not mandatory; the block ends and the user builds the next; holidays and vacations sit between blocks.

**Sport dial and populations**: swimming dryland (3 days + 1 optional, 25 % plyo, 0 extra cardio, shoulder care every session, Olympic lifts 2-3 days, taper with the swim taper); older adults (60+) landing drills, balance, quick stepping, light medball throws and fast machine work on, ankle hops / other jumps / Olympic lifts / depth jumps off by default; pickleball, padel and tennis players 50+ calf and Achilles work every leg day, rotator cuff, low-impact jumps; HYROX plan; the R3-ATH-04 plyo shares for every remaining sport; stay-active play days, activity sessions as cardio, event dates.
**Questions**: 11.3 questions on the grouping, the field-athlete layout, swimming, pickleball 60+, rear delts / check-in and the floor at the start are answered; new questions 11.4.

pairing.rule: In any session that mixes lower and upper work, a hip-dominant (posterior lower) pattern is paired with a push (anterior upper) and a knee-dominant pattern with a pull (posterior upper). The coach's reason: keep paired work as far apart as possible so fatigue does not bleed over, which lets the client do more total work across the week. Applies to full body, bootcamps, athletic days, strength compressions and hybrid days (ORD-06: 'That's the model that I'm using for full bodies and for boot camps').
pairing.level: slot level: each upper compound carries pair = P1/P2/P3 with its lower pattern and must satisfy the rule (checked in every generated template). Day-level counting (v0 '20 of 23') is retired.

same_pattern.what: bilateral + unilateral of the SAME dominance on one day (squat + lunge; hinge + single-leg hinge); the day then carries both pulls (knee day) or both pushes (hip day)

It reaches 2 per muscle with fewer exercises than the cross pattern, so it fits the field-athlete cap more easily (R2-SES-04).

supersets_and_complexes.generator_rule: Supersets are a fatigue and time tool (ORD-05). Use them when: (1) the session is short (30-45 min, or when added sets push a session past its length); (2) an advanced (L3) athlete or lifter needs more stimulus - the superset compresses the fatigue; (3) athletes in the off-season working on VO2max and mitochondrial capacity; (4) a beginner (L1) who is not getting fatigued by straight sets. An intermediate (L2) with enough time trains straight sets by default (INFERRED from the four cases). What to pair: the UNI-11 pairs (knee lift + pull, hip lift + push) and isolation pairs (e.g. biceps + rear delts, triceps + side delts, calves + delts). Never two lower compounds; never a heavy lift with a fatiguing lift for the same muscle, except contrast/French contrast for L2+ athletes off-season at about 78-85% with no rest inside the complex (ATH-12). Athletic families may use the BASEBALL grammar (Part C = bilateral lower + one upper compound, 'Superset - same reps'; Part D = unilateral + two isolations). Hybrid sessions do the paired accessory in the strength lift's rest period (OBSERVED HYBRID tri-sets).

Athletic off-season pairs are supersetted (ORD-05 VO2max / mitochondrial case). Core supersets and monster sets are optional add-ons anywhere (R2-SES-03).

A muscle group is never cut to one exercise (R2-SES-05); a whole group may move to the optional day only on request.

deload_test_architecture.architecture_rule: OBSERVED v0 reading (BASEBALL 'DELOAD WEEK'): deloads keep the session architecture - same slots, fewer sets, lighter reps; the buy-out and the Oly piece were absent. Where this differs from v1_rule (PER-05: about half the sets, same exercises, lighter or 3+ RIR, no buy-out or finisher), v1_rule governs; dropping the Olympic piece in a deload is OBSERVED, not a coach rule. v1.1: the deload week itself is retired inside blocks (R2-VOL-07); this reading now describes the maintenance phase.
deload_test_architecture.v1_rule: HISTORY (v1; superseded by v1_1_rule - its deload week inside a block, the '8-week = 4 + 4, start hard' and the '12-week = 2-4 weeks acclimation' shapes are retired by COACH-R2 R2-VOL-07 and R2-PER-03/04): Deload (PER-05): same exercises and architecture, about half the sets, lighter load or 3+ RIR, no buy-out or finisher. Tests (PER-07): chosen by checkbox at block start (strength, cardio, speed, or 'no need for testing'); when chosen, the final week holds a test day in place of one session. Plan shapes (PER-01, details in 06): 4-6 week maintenance/transition blocks at about 50-70% volume on the same templates; 8-week = 4 weeks adapting + 4 weeks driving hard, start hard; 12-week (preferred) = 2-4 weeks acclimation, 4-6 weeks hard, hardest last weeks; repeated 12-week cycles start one level higher; open week-by-week mode; yearly mode with quarter themes and holiday weeks in maintenance.
deload_test_architecture.retired_v0_rules: v0 '8 weeks = 7 building + week 8 test/deload', '12 weeks = 6 + deload + 5' and '6 weeks = 5 + deload/test' are retired by COACH-ANSWER PER-01 (NOT RIGHT). 4-6 week plans are maintenance / transition at about 50-70% volume; 8-week = 4 adapting + 4 driving hard; 12-week = 2-4 acclimation + 4-6 hard + hardest last weeks (details in 06). [v1.1: these v1 replacement shapes are themselves retired - every plan length is a stairway with the hardest weeks last and no deload inside a block (COACH-R2 R2-PER-03/04, R2-VOL-07); see v1_1_rule.]
deload_test_architecture.v1_1_rule: No deload or maintenance week inside a block: a block is completed (COACH-R2 R2-VOL-07: maintenance 'should never be thrown in the middle of a block'). If a client cannot complete it, the block is cancelled, a maintenance phase follows, and then a whole new block starts. Maintenance = same templates at about 50-70% of the sets (PER-01), same exercises, 3+ RIR, no buy-out or finisher (PER-05); its length is chosen and can be extended; at its end the plan asks: keep maintaining / change the plan / start a training block (R2-PER-06). Pre-season = a 4-6-week block at about 60% of off-season sets with more speed and power + a 1-2-week taper (R2-PER-06). Every plan length is a stairway: smaller steps first, slightly bigger after halfway, the hardest weeks last (12-week: the last 4 weeks 'brutal'); 'start at a 2, end at an 11' is perceived effort / overall load, not set counts (R2-PER-03/04/05). Tests before the block (or in week 1) and at the end, never mid-block - the end test takes the place of that week's top sets (R2-PER-07 proposal, approved); untrained people never test a 1RM or a max mile from zero - 5RM / 3RM or 80-90% efforts (R2-PER-07). Details in 06.
deload_test_architecture.v1_2_rule: COACH-R3 PER-01 (RIGHT): 'maintenance weeks are a recommendation. They don't have to be mandatory ... when the block ends, it just ends, and then you have to go back into the app and build whatever you want next.' The easy week after a block (about half of the hardest week) is recommended, never forced; maintenance has no end prompt (the plan just ends; nothing is stored, COACH-R3 GEN-01); holidays and vacations are planned between blocks; tests stay before / at the end and are printed in the plan (no reminders). No deload or maintenance inside a block (R2-VOL-07); the in-block check-in tools are retired (COACH-R3 VOL-02).
deload_test_architecture.v1_1_rule_status_v1_2: history: its 'cancelled -> a maintenance phase follows' and the end prompt ('keep maintaining / change the plan / start a training block') changed in v1.2 - maintenance is optional and the plan just ends (COACH-R3 PER-01, GEN-01)

laterality_dial.status: COACH-ANSWER UNI-02, UNI-03, UNI-10, UNI-08, CAT-13 (ranges and logic); default shares beyond his anchor points PROPOSED; the set math lives in 12_volume_algorithm_v1
laterality_dial.rule: Each lower (and upper) compound slot names a dominance; its laterality (bilateral or unilateral) is chosen so that the week's bilateral:unilateral share of sets matches the client's dial. Range 90/10 to 10/90. Unilateral work = health and rotational foundation; bilateral work = the driving force for size and strength.

anchors.bodybuilders / powerlifters: about 50/50 at the start of a program, moving to 80/20 - 90/10 bilateral; contralateral/ipsilateral unilateral work as health accessories mostly in the first 2-4 weeks, kept later only if something bothers them (UNI-02, CAT-13)
anchors.pain or injury: adjust accordingly; swapping a painful bilateral for a unilateral keeps the sets 'ideally' but is adjusted case by case (UNI-08, UNI-02)

laterality_dial.contra_ipsi: contralateral load pulls the athlete INTO the hip (COD athletes: football, soccer, basketball, tennis); ipsilateral helps OUT of the hip (sprint acceleration, e.g. ipsilateral step-ups) (CAT-13)
laterality_dial.slot_conversion: PROPOSED: convert bilateral stations to unilateral stations of the same dominance, starting with the second weekly exposure, until the share matches; keep at least one bilateral exposure a week off-season unless pain or in-season says otherwise.

axial_loading.rule: Load the spine once a week per pattern and load it correctly: one axial squat exposure and one axial hinge exposure a week. The second weekly squat exposure is a leg press or belt squat; deadlifts load the spine too, so the second hinge exposure is non-axial.
axial_loading.coach_words: 'I can do one day of squatting and the other day of leg pressing. I don't want to always load the lower back and the spine twice per week.' (PER-04)

set_addition.status: COACH-ANSWER VOL-07 (order), VOL-06 (rounding), VOL-04/VOL-05; COACH-R2 R2-VOL-04/06 (floor 10 sets per muscle per week, small muscles the same idea), R2-VOL-08 (default chosen - the coach did not understand the question), R2-SES-05; COACH-R3 VOL-03 (RIGHT: day alternation and bonus placement), VOL-04 (stairway approved), VOL-02 (no check-in), VOL-01 (shoulders group), SES-01 (Focus muscles)

set_addition.order: when a muscle needs +1 set, add it to the FIRST exercise for that muscle in session order; the next added set goes to the second, then the third, then back to the first: 2/2/2 -> 3/2/2 -> 3/3/2 -> 3/3/3 -> 4/3/3 (equivalently: the exercise with the fewest sets, earliest first)
set_addition.why: 'I'm adding sets to the things that matter most... usually in the beginning... because I put all my energy into it' (VOL-07)
set_addition.small_muscle_bonus: v1.2 (COACH-R3 VOL-03, approved): a small muscle's extra sets become a short bonus exercise (2 sets, same category) 'on the optional day (e.g. Saturday); with no optional day, on a day that already trains biceps, never as the only biceps exercise of that day'; calves never get a second calf exercise on a leg day (R3-SES-01)
set_addition.weekly_rate: v1.2: the planned stairway is approved (COACH-R3 VOL-04): about 3 % a week to the halfway week, about 5 % after it, every trained line on its ceiling in the last week, effort 3 RIR -> 2 -> 1-2 -> 1 RIR + intensifiers; the whole plan is computed once - no check-in, nothing stored (COACH-R3 VOL-02, GEN-01). Engine in 12_volume_algorithm.
set_addition.two_sessions_of_the_same_day_type: approved (COACH-R3 VOL-03): when a day type appears twice a week (A1 Monday, A2 Thursday), added sets alternate - 'the back set goes to Monday's first back exercise this time and Thursday's first back exercise the next time, so both days stay even'
set_addition.pseudo: def add_set(day, muscle): ex = [e for e in day.exercises if e.primary == muscle]; target = min(ex, key=lambda e: (e.sets, e.position)); target.sets += 1
set_addition.floor_R2VOL04: no trained group below 10 weekly sets ('I don't think anybody needs less than 10'); small muscles follow the same idea (COACH-R2 R2-VOL-04/06). v1.2: the floor is read on groups - quads, hips, chest, back, shoulders, biceps, triceps, calves - with group credit; rear delts are part of the shoulders group (their own 4 / 6 / 8 retired; a rear-delt exercise every week; 'add rear delts' in the plan editor) (COACH-R3 VOL-01, SES-01). The volume engine (12 v1.2) owns the numbers
set_addition.caps_R2VOL06: caps approved and customizable; most people train 20-30 sets per muscle per week; above 30 only for very advanced lifters - an optional coach 'Pro' setting may let a Focus or priority muscle pass 30 (COACH-R2 R2-VOL-06; numbers owned by 12)
set_addition.floor_vs_template_start: the templates' sets_hint (2 per exercise, the second small-muscle exercise 1 below 90 min) is the per-station starting dose, not the weekly start. Where a week built at that dose leaves a trained muscle below 10 sets (R2-VOL-04/06) - mostly 2-3-day plans, upper/lower, arms in 4-6-day same-pattern weeks, and the CrossFit / hybrid class model - the volume engine (12) adds the missing sets in week 1 by the VOL-07 order, so those block-start days run longer than checks.est_minutes_start. Recomputed per template in rules.floor10_start_check_R2VOL06 (v1.1 adversarial check).
set_addition.focus_muscles_R3SES01: Focus muscle 1 and Focus muscle 2 (none, one or two lines): +1 to +3 weekly sets each (default +2, PROPOSED - PENDING COACH APPROVAL) on start and ceiling, first in their session, delivered through their own exercises, then the optional-day Focus slots, then a bonus exercise; they do not slow the other lines (COACH-R3 SES-01)

science_notes: SCIENCE: per-set durations assume 30-60 s of work and the coach's own rests (1-2 min hypertrophy, 3-6 min strength); agonist-antagonist / non-competing pairing roughly halves rest overhead without hurting volume load (Robbins et al. 2010, JSCR; Weakley et al. 2017, EJAP; Iversen et al. 2021, Sports Med)

SCIENCE (weak): a per-session ceiling of roughly 6-10 hard sets per muscle is an RP practitioner heuristic with limited direct trial evidence; Schoenfeld et al. 2017 is a WEEKLY dose-response meta-analysis and does not support a per-session cap. The coach's habit of adding other qualities to long sessions is OBSERVED behaviour, not derived from this.

SCIENCE: exercise order effects - movements done first get more reps and quality (Simao et al. 2012, Sports Med), supporting 'priority first' (athletic first; calves/delts first when they are the priority)

SCIENCE: per-session sets per muscle - the dose-response for hypertrophy flattens within a session at around 6-11 hard sets per muscle (practitioner landmarks; weak direct trial evidence). Same-pattern days (squat + lunge + leg extension) put 8-11 quad sets in one session at 90 min, which sits inside that range; the volume engine (12) owns the weekly numbers.

aesthetics.family_notes: Muscle & physique. SAME-pattern days (squat + lunge; hinge + single-leg hinge) to drive the muscle harder (COACH-ANSWER UNI-06). Knee days carry the pulls, hip days the pushes (UNI-11). v1.1: every muscle group a full-body day trains gets 2-4 exercises, never 1 (COACH-R2 R2-SES-05) - knee day: quads 3, back 2, shoulders 2 (rear delt + KB face pull, R2-LIB-04), biceps 2, calves 1 (3 sets); hip day: hips 3, chest 2, shoulders 2, triceps 2, calves 1 (3 sets). Days start short (2 sets per exercise) and lengthen as sets are added. Core opens light (2 x 2, R2-SES-03). Heavy squat Monday, heavy deadlift Friday (R2-SES-01). Session 60 min for general clients, about 90 min for bodybuilders (UNI-09). No medball except as warm-up (ATH-05). Aerobic: 4 a week (Blue, Green, Orange + a second easy Orange) + optional 20-30-min walks after workouts, adjustable by the user (COACH-R2 R2-SES-06). v1.2: calves one exercise x 3 sets per leg day (R3-SES-01); every main day lists recommended supersets and block toggles (R3-SES-02).

athletic.family_notes: Field / court / combat / aquatic athletes and non-competitive athletic adults and youth ('Athletic Performance', renamed from 'JUSTICE LEAGUE', ATH-13 / FIX-03; the gen-pop 'stay athletic and active' path - pickleball, tennis, golf, rec leagues - uses the non-competitive version). CROSS-pattern days by default (squat + single-leg hinge; UNI-06); SAME-pattern variant for high-level athletes who need more stimulus (UNI-06). v1.1: every muscle group a day trains gets 2-4 exercises (COACH-R2 R2-SES-05) inside the field-athlete cap of 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block (R2-SES-04: warm-up drills never count, a superset of two small isolations counts as one). With the cross pattern that leaves room for 2 plyo/ballistic stations + 1 Olympic lift; the same-pattern variant needs fewer resistance exercises and keeps 3-4 athletic stations. Olympic work on every main day - clean days = squat days, snatch days = hinge days (R2-ATH-04). Older adults (60+): no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default; optional with the W_OLDER_POWER warning (R2-ATH-08). Athletic patterns never count toward muscle sets (VOL-10). About 90 min competitive (max 2 h), 60 min non-competitive (UNI-09; PROPOSED). In season: 2 days, minimal bilateral (UNI-10, PER-08), game-heavy reductions (R2-ATH-07). v1.2: calves one exercise x 3 sets per leg day (R3-SES-01); every main day lists recommended supersets and block toggles (R3-SES-02).

sport_dial.ground_contact_model: The longer a sport keeps the athlete on the ground, the more ballistics and the fewer plyos; the shorter, the more plyos (ATH-01). Both ends are always present. Programs start more ballistic and become more plyometric over the block (CAT-10).

fat_loss_bootcamp.family_notes: Weight loss / general fitness / bootcamp. CROSS-pattern sessions so clients stay less sore and can train more often (COACH-ANSWER UNI-06); hinge + push and squat + pull in every session (UNI-11, ORD-06). v1.1: every muscle group the day trains gets 2 exercises (COACH-R2 R2-SES-05) - the second one is a lighter isolation or bodyweight option of the same group (the coach's own cross day already adds leg extensions to the squat day, OBSERVED OT05), so the cross pattern keeps soreness spread. Two formats: GYM (straight sets, 45-60 min, UNI-09; full-body days run about 60 min at the start) and BOOTCAMP CIRCUIT (two circuits of 4-6 stations, 3 rounds x 35-50 s, 35-45 min, 4/5/6 sessions a week - PRG-03 + R2-SES-05). 3 aerobic sessions a week (ATH-07), adjustable up or down by the user (R2-SES-06). Fat loss is muscle building plus energy balance ('MUSCLE BUILDING' header in FAT BURN, OBSERVED). v1.2: calves one exercise x 3 sets per leg day (R3-SES-01); every main day lists recommended supersets and block toggles (R3-SES-02).

hybrid_crossfit.family_notes: Strength + Olympic + conditioning (CrossFit-style class, CrossFit-style bootcamp, HYROX-style fitness). Class order: warm-up -> light core block (R2-SES-03) -> skill -> Olympic/power -> strength (+ its accessories) -> WOD (OBSERVED OT18 'WARMUP/SKILL' -> 'STRENGTH/POWER' -> 'WOD'; ATH-11, ORD-03). v1.1 class model: each day trains one strength pattern and its paired upper group with 2 exercises each (R2-SES-05) plus calves on leg days; the WOD carries the conditioning. Levels (OBSERVED OT17): HALF TIME = class member (strength 3x7 -> 3x6 -> 3x5 -> 3x4 -> L5 work up to a 1RM; power 3x4 -> 3x1), FULL TIME = competitor (strength 3x7 -> 6x4; power 3x3 -> 6x3); WOD level 1-4 = 1-4 WODs a week; aerobic level 1-4 = C; C,B; C,B,A; + lactate clearance. A 1RM test only at the end of a completed block (R2-PER-07). 40-rep sets and AMRAPs live here only (VOL-11). Heavy squat and heavy deadlift on different days (R2-SES-01). v1.2: calves one exercise x 3 sets per leg day (R3-SES-01); every main day lists recommended supersets and block toggles (R3-SES-02).
hybrid_crossfit.pairing_mode: class model (one strength pattern + its UNI-11 upper group per day)

generator_algorithm: 1 INPUTS (after the health screen and release - v1.2, COACH-R3 GEN-01: a short Blaze Camp health check in English and Spanish written by a lawyer, with a link to the official PAR-Q+; a coach may run it with the client or skip it after the Blaze Camp legal warning; everyone ticks the 'use at your own risk' box and accepts the terms and conditions and liability release every time a plan is built; nothing is stored; drafts in DISCLAIMER.md / DISCLAIMER.es.md; flow owned by the generator spec / 13; R2-GEN-03's 'PAR-Q for clients' superseded): goal family; days per week (2-6); session minutes (45/60/75/90; PROPOSED 105/120 for competitive athletes, UNI-09); level L1/L2/L3 (PRG-05); equipment; competitive athletes: sport + position + season start date (or 'in season until') + practice and game days (GEN-02, COACH-R2 R2-GEN-05); recreational 'stay athletic and active': activity only (pickleball, HYROX, ...); age (60+ rules, R2-ATH-08); plan type (block length / maintenance / year, PER-01, R2-PER-01/02; week-by-week retired, R3-VOL-02); Focus muscle 1 and Focus muscle 2 (+1-3 sets each, R3-SES-01); play days and an optional event date for stay-active users (R3-ATH-05); blocks completed in a row when rebuilding (PROPOSED; nothing is stored, R3-GEN-01); pain areas; rep-style preference; more/less cardio (R2-SES-06); coach-added rules (GEN-08). NO sleep, stress or lifestyle fields (COACH-R2 R2-GEN-04).

2 WEEK: take generator_split_templates[family][days].week_layout, or the variant the sport, phase or preference selects (same-pattern athletic, BASEBALL Parts, in-season keyed to game days, upper/lower, PPL x2, bootcamp circuit, CrossFit-style bootcamp). Heavy squat Monday, heavy deadlift Friday, non-axial hinge Tuesday, leg press / belt squat Thursday (R2-SES-01). Optional days separate by default (ORD-10). Place aerobic sessions by population and adjust them to the user's more/less request (ATH-07, R2-SES-06, R2-ATH-06).

3 SESSIONS: keep stations with include_from_minutes <= minutes; drop stations whose condition is false (Focus calves, powerlifter technique lift); keep each station's block id and drop the blocks the user switched off for that day (R3-SES-02); for 60+ clients drop stations marked older_default unless switched on (then show W_OLDER_POWER, R2-ATH-08); warm-up always (ORD-08); light core block first unless moved (ATH-11, R2-SES-03); optional core supersets / monster sets where the user or coach adds them (R2-SES-03).

4 PAIRING + SUPERSETS: keep the UNI-11 pairs (hip + push, knee + pull) incl. the second-exercise pairs; superset them when the session is short, for L3 athletes who need more stimulus, for off-season athletes (VO2max / mitochondrial work) or for L1 clients who do not fatigue (ORD-05); small-isolation pairs are always supersets. v1.2: the plan lists every eligible pair as a recommended superset, "needed" when the day fits only with it (R3-SES-02).

5 ORDER: warm-up -> core block -> (skill) -> plyo/ballistic -> throws -> COD -> Olympic/power (ORD-03; clean on squat days, snatch on hinge days, R2-ATH-04) -> the work + paired upper -> secondary pairs (H before V, ORD-01) -> each group's second exercise -> isolation (small muscle first only if it is a Focus muscle (R3-SES-01), ORD-04) -> conditioning / WOD.

6 VALIDATE THE WEEK: 2-4 exercises per muscle group trained each day (R2-SES-05); pattern frequency; slot-level pairing; axial budget <= 1 heavy squat + 1 heavy hinge on different days (PER-04, R2-SES-01/02); each upper vector >= 1x; exactly one calf exercise x 3 sets every leg day (R3-SES-01); >= 1 rear-delt / face-pull station a week (VOL-17); field-athlete cap 12 + 2 core with small-isolation supersets counted once (R2-SES-04); time at block start and late block; >= 1 OFF day; coach-added rules (GEN-08). v1.2: the time-vs-minimums check (R3-SES-02): at week 1 with the floor and at the peak week, every eligible pair supersetted, each day <= the chosen length x 1.10; otherwise tell up front + offer.

7 FILL: default exercise per slot + swaps in the same category (GEN-04); only library exercises - between blocks one detail may change (hand, grip, stance, implement, range), never an invented exercise (R2-LIB-01); filter by level (CAT-05), equipment (no bands / variable resistance, EQ-01, EQ-12), pain (VOL-03), preference (EQ-10), older/injured constrained machines (EQ-03), 60+ power defaults (R2-ATH-08); second weekly exposure = different exercise, non-axial for squats and hinges (PER-04, R2-SES-02); KB face pulls as shoulder work (R2-LIB-04); laterality dial (UNI-02).

8 DOSE: starting weekly sets from the volume engine (12): floor 10 per trained group with group credit (R2-VOL-04/06; R3-VOL-01, SES-01); Focus muscles +1-3 (R3-SES-01), caps customizable (R2-VOL-06); credit the exercise picked: primary 1.0, helpers 0.25 (VOL-09), compounds 0.25 glutes, thruster 1.0 quads / 0.5 shoulders / 0.25 glutes, KB swings 0 (R2-VOL-05), dips 0.5/0.5 (LIB-16), 10/10 = 1 set (UNI-01), athletic patterns 0 (VOL-10); effort by RIR / RPE (VOL-13, R2-GEN-06; effort 10 = the max I could do, successful - R2-VOL-02); Olympic lifts by power output, % only with a tested recent best, %-driven programming only for competitive Olympic lifters (R2-GEN-06).

9 PROGRESS: the approved planned stairway (R2-PER-03/04/05; COACH-R3 VOL-04), computed once - no check-in, nothing stored (COACH-R3 VOL-02, GEN-01) - adds sets by the VOL-07 order (2/2/2 -> 3/2/2 -> 3/3/2 -> 3/3/3 -> 4/3/3), alternating between the two weekly exposures of a day type (approved, COACH-R3 VOL-03); a small muscle's bonus exercise on the optional day or a day that already trains it; calves never a second exercise on a leg day (R3-SES-01). TIME (COACH-R3 SES-02): if the chosen time cannot hold the minimums, tell up front and offer another day or a longer session; if the user keeps the time, train fewer groups directly, recommend supersets, and let the stairway climb on every trained group - never squeeze 2-4 exercises per group into a day that cannot hold them. Print the self-adjust guide (12 section 3.7.3).

10 PERIODISE (details in 06): blocks are completed - no deload or maintenance week inside a block (R2-VOL-07); the easy week after a block (about half the hardest week) is a recommendation, not mandatory; the block ends and the user builds the next (COACH-R3 PER-01); maintenance has no end prompt; holidays and vacations between blocks; pre-season 4-6 weeks at ~60% with more speed and power + 1-2-week taper; tests before the block (or week 1) and at the end, printed in the plan, never mid-block, no 1RM / max mile from zero (R2-PER-07); between blocks change one or two small variables (PER-02, R2-LIB-01); gen-pop year plan fully user-tunable (R2-PER-01/02).

new_v1_1_questions: PER-MUSCLE COUNT (R2-SES-05): we count glutes and hamstrings as one group ('hips') and side, rear and front delts + traps as one ('shoulders'), so a hip day with a deadlift, a single-leg RDL and a leg curl meets '2-4 per muscle'. Should glutes and hamstrings each get their own 2 exercises (one more exercise on hip days)?

CROSS-PATTERN DAYS (UNI-06 + R2-SES-05): to give every muscle 2 exercises while keeping squat + single-leg RDL on the same day, the second exercise of each lower group is a lighter one (leg extension after the squat, leg curl after the single-leg RDL), like your BOOTCAMP 1 A day. That makes a 45-60-min bootcamp / fat-loss gym day about 10 exercises (~51 min at 45, ~60 at 60 at the start). OK, or should these clients use knee days and hip days (fewer exercises, but quads and hamstrings on different days)?

BOOTCAMP CIRCUITS (PRG-03 + R2-SES-05): 2 stations per muscle gives 9-11 stations. We split them into two circuits of 4-6 stations (3 rounds x 35-50 s, ~43-45 min). OK, or one 7-station circuit that trains fewer muscles per day?

FIELD-ATHLETE CAP (R2-SES-04 + R2-SES-05): with the cross pattern, 2 exercises per muscle uses 9 of the 12 slots, leaving 2 plyo/ballistic stations + 1 Olympic lift. Your own BYOP athletic template (same pattern) needs fewer, leaving 3-4 + 1. Keep cross pattern as the athlete default, or use your same-pattern template for off-season athletes?

CONJUGATE STRENGTH DAYS (ORD-07 + R2-SES-05): your four-role days give some muscles one exercise (e.g. the max-effort lower day: one hinge accessory, one pull). Keep them as you wrote them, or add a second exercise per muscle like the other plans?
IN-SEASON DAYS (R2-SES-05 + PER-08): 2 exercises per muscle in season makes the 2 gym days about 12 exercises at 1-2 sets (~56-65 min). OK, or should in-season days train fewer muscles?
SWIMMING (R2-GEN-07 sample): dryland around pool training - is 0-1 gym aerobic session a week right (the pool covers it), and how many dryland days for age-group / high-school / college swimmers?

PICKLEBALL 50+ / 60+ (new request): for recreational pickleball players over 60 we keep plyos and Olympic lifts off by default (R2-ATH-08) and use landing drills, low ankle hops and lateral split-step drills. Right?

REAR DELTS AND THE CHECK-IN (R2-VOL-04 vs R2-VOL-06; R2-VOL-01 vs R2-GEN-04): rear delts keep their approved 4 / 6 / 8 own sets while the floor of 10 is read on the whole shoulders/traps group - OK? And the approved check-in table had a 'life' column, which we dropped because you said 'no need to talk about sleep or stress' - OK?

FLOOR OF 10 AT THE START (R2-VOL-04/06 + R2-SES-05): with 2 sets per exercise, 2-3-day plans, upper/lower weeks and the CrossFit-style class give some muscles only 2-9 sets in week 1, so the floor adds sets and the first days get longer (e.g. a 2-day full-body day ~60 -> ~72 min, a 2-day fat-loss day ~60 -> ~83, a CrossFit-style class ~68 -> ~90; rules.floor10_start_check_R2VOL06).
